The one entry here that is a DELIBERATE reduction rather than an addition, and it is allowlisted on a different invariant. Its fragments are a header plus 'Reading what you caught…' — two sentences that say the same thing twice and re-speak on every focus event during a multi-second wait. One short sentence naming the blocking operation is the correct utterance for a modal veil. The `.accessibilityIdentifier("captureAnalyzing")` on the next line is what the UI suites query, so shortening the label broke nothing.

Adds the CAPTION-TO-VALUE relation. The fragments are a slot caption and a value drawn one above the other; `.combine` speaks them as two unlinked items in one breath, and the widget slot rows stack several of them, so a user hears four captions and four values with no way to pair them. The colon is what carries the pairing in speech. `Text(slot)` rather than `slot` is deliberate and commented at the site: a `LocalizedStringKey` cannot be interpolated into another `LocalizedStringKey`, but a `Text` carries its own lookup.

Adds the AUTHOR. `.combine` gathers a chat bubble's fragments, which are a sender-name caption plus the message text for an INCOMING message and the message text ALONE for an outgoing one — the name caption is drawn only under `if !message.isOutgoing` (:103). So an outgoing bubble combines to the bare sentence with nothing saying who sent it; authorship is carried purely by right-alignment and the terracotta tint, and neither of those is speech. The label restores it ('You: …') and supplies the speaker-to-utterance colon on the incoming branch. This site was invisible to the wall until the 2026-08-23 A1 hardening: `.accessibilityIdentifier("session.chat.message")` sits BETWEEN `.combine` and the label, and the old rule inspected only the immediately-next code line — this is the review's planted evasion #3 (one interleaved modifier) occurring naturally in shipping code, and surfacing it is the hardening working.
